transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what's been going on that brought you in today?

Hi, thank you. Well, what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I keep getting up during things when I know I really should just stay put. 

Like, during sprint planning for work, or even important personal things like mortgage calls. I know I need to stay at my desk, but I'll just... suddenly decide I need to go get a glass of water, or I'll get up to check something in the other room. It's been happening enough lately that I felt I should come in and talk to someone about it.
When you get up during these situations, do you feel a sudden, almost irresistible urge to move or act, or does it feel more like a habit or something you just decide to do without much thought?

It's definitely more of an urge. Um, it's like... even if I'm sitting there and I probably look completely calm on the outside, I get this intense pressure inside. 

It just feels like I need to move, or switch to a different task, or at least do something with my hands. If I don't, it builds up and I feel like I'm going to crawl out of my skin. So, yeah, it's not really a habit or a casual decision, it's more of a physical feeling that I just have to do something right then.
Do these urges to move or act happen most of the time, even when you're not in structured situations like meetings, such as when you're trying to relax or read something quietly?

Yeah, it does. Um, like I was just saying about that pressure... it doesn't really turn off just because I'm off the clock. 

If I'm trying to read a book or watch TV on the weekend, I might look like I'm just sitting there calmly on the couch, but I still get that exact same feeling. I'll just feel like I need to get up, or switch to doing something else, or at least fiddle with something in my hands. It's that same feeling of needing to move before I crawl out of my skin, just... happening during my downtime, too. So, yeah, it's pretty much most of the time.
When you feel that pressure or urge to move, does it happen specifically in your legs, and does moving them give you a sense of relief?

No, it's not really just in my legs. I mean, my legs might feel restless, but the feeling is more... all over. It's just a general sense of being on edge and needing to do something. Moving around does help relieve it a little bit, but it's not like a specific itch in my legs that I'm scratching. It's more of a full-body restlessness.
Looking back, were you also someone who had trouble staying still or felt restless as a child, or did this start more recently as an adult?

It definitely started when I was a kid. Um, I remember back in elementary school, my teachers were always having to remind me to stay seated. They actually had to move my desk a few times because I was just always popping up out of my chair. I'd also talk before I was called on, or I'd just rush through my assignments, even when I completely understood the work. So, yeah, that restlessness isn't a new thing for me, it's pretty much always been there.
